label: Figure 18.1: The effect of supply-side policies
alt: Two panels. (a) A Keynesian-shaped short-run aggregate supply curve, flat at low output and vertical at full capacity, shifts right from AS1 to AS2. (b) A vertical long-run aggregate supply curve shifts right from LRAS1 to LRAS2. Both axes show average price level against real output.
caption: Supply-side policies raise the economy’s productive capacity. Panel (a): the Keynesian aggregate supply curve, flat while there is spare capacity and vertical at full capacity, moves right from AS1 to AS2, so full-capacity output rises. Panel (b): in the long-run (classical) model the vertical LRAS shifts right from LRAS1 to LRAS2, showing a higher potential level of real output.
